title: Salade Nicoise
subtitle: Classic Provencal salad with tuna, egg, and olives
excerpt: This is a composed salad rather than a tossed one -- each component is arranged rather than mixed, which keeps the textures distinct. The dressing is a simple vinaigrette, not a thick sauce, and should be made sharp enough to cut through the richness of the tuna and egg yolk.
sourceNotes: Salade nicoise originated in Nice and has been a source of culinary debate for over a century. Auguste Escoffier and later Jacques Medecin both published versions, with Medecin insisting that cooked vegetables, particularly potatoes and green beans, should never appear in an authentic nicoise. Most home-cook versions include them.

content.text: Hard-boiled eggs for this salad need 9 minutes in simmering water, not a full rolling boil -- a slightly jammy yolk is better than a chalky one. Plunge them into cold water immediately to stop the cooking.

Simmer the eggs in water for 9 minutes, then transfer immediately to cold water. Boil the potatoes until just tender -- about 12-15 minutes. Blanch the green beans in salted boiling water for 3 minutes and refresh under cold water.
Make the dressing: whisk the dijon mustard and red wine vinegar together, then whisk in the olive oil in a steady stream. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel and halve the eggs. Arrange the potatoes, green beans, tomato wedges, and black olives across a large platter or individual plates.
Flake the tuna over the top. Add the egg halves and anchovy fillets. Drizzle the dressing over everything and serve.

items.cause: Oil added too fast or not whisked long enough.
items.fix: Add the olive oil very slowly at first, whisking constantly. A tight vinaigrette comes together in about 60 seconds of steady whisking.
